claims: TPSM restores laboratory rotational symmetry by 3D angular-momentum projection from deformed Nilsson+BCS multi-quasiparticle bases, solving the Hill-Wheeler equation without cranking approximations.

Short-axis quantization (gamma -> -120 deg - gamma) microscopically reveals that the yrast band is dominated by K=11/2 along the s-axis, while the excited wobbling band has K=7/2, directly demonstrating off-axis tilted precession.

TSD nuclei (161-167Lu, 167Ta) exhibit TW with identical alignments and dynamic moments of inertia between doublet bands, satisfying the harmonic multi-phonon selection rule B(E2; n=2 -> 1) ~ 2 x B(E2; n=1 -> 0) with forbidden n=2 -> 0 cross-phonon transitions.
Normal deformed 10 nuclei are classified into TW, LW and inflection categories with enhanced B(E2)out/B(E2)in and suppressed B(M1).
TPSM provides a unified microscopic description that distinguishes collective wobbling bands from single-particle signature partner bands within the same Hamiltonian.
